adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:354 — With skipToken (non-Grafana/datasource or legacy cloud rules), useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported and Duplicate resolves to [true, hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)]. The OR in AlertRuleMenu then shows Duplicate for Mimir/Loki/Prometheus rules even when the ruler path denies it (no ruler, or no external write permission).

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows AlertRuleMenu now ORs abilities from useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities. For non-Grafana prom rules it passes `skipToken` (AlertRuleMenu.tsx), which `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` converts to `undefined` and still calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, when `rule` is undefined, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `{isEditable:false,isRemovable:false,loading:false}`, making `MaybeSupported = AlwaysSupported` (not NotSupported). Since `isPluginProvidedRule(undefined)` likely yields false, `duplicateSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported`, and `Duplicate` becomes supported based only on `getRulesPermissions('grafana').create`. This makes the Grafana-prom ability path report Duplicate as supported/allowed even when the rule is not Grafana-managed, and because AlertRuleMenu ORs the two paths, the menu can incorrectly expose actions (e.g., Duplicate) for datasource/cloud rules when the ruler ability path denies them.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:245 — useAllAlertRuleAbilities (CombinedRule, used by the legacy list/RuleDetails) hardcodes isFederated=false where it used to call isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group), so federated Mimir rule groups become editable and deletable again.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `useAllAlertRuleAbilities` to delegate to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities(...)`, and inside `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` the federated check is now hardcoded: `const isFederated = false;` with the previous `isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` logic removed (import of `isFederatedRuleGroup` is deleted and the old `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` usage is gone). Since `immutableRule` depends on `isFederated`, this can re-enable Update/Delete/Duplicate/etc. for federated rule groups that were previously treated as immutable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:165 — Delete is still gated on `rulerRule`, so in the new list view (promRule only) Delete never shows even when the promRule ability grants it; this is a silent functional regression.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly refactors `AlertRuleMenu` to compute `canDelete` from both ruler- and prom-based abilities: it calls `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)`, then sets `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`. This means Delete is no longer solely gated on `rulerRule`; when only `promRule` is available (and is a Grafana Prom rule), the prom ability can enable Delete. The finding claiming Delete “never shows” in the promRule-only list view is contradicted by the new logic shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 — Pause/Resume is still gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule), so it is never shown in the new list view even though canPause is computed from promRule.

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows the refactor of ability checks (introducing useRulerRuleAbilities/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and computing canPause as an OR), but it does not include the later JSX/conditional rendering section around the claimed line (~123) where Pause/Resume would be gated on rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule). Since that gating code is not shown/changed in this diff, the specific claim that Pause/Resume is "still gated" cannot be verified from the provided diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:207 — The test asserts exactly 4 menu items for a user with update/delete permissions, which locks in the missing Delete and Pause items instead of catching them.

adjudication.rationale: In `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, the “should render correct menu actions when More button is clicked” test grants update/delete permissions in `beforeEach` (e.g., `AlertingRuleDelete` and folder access control), defines a `delete` selector in `ui.menuItems`, but then only asserts Silence/Copy link/Duplicate/Export and finally hard-codes `expect(menuItems.length).toBe(4)`. This makes the test brittle and effectively encodes that no Delete (and any other action like Pause) should appear, rather than explicitly asserting presence/absence based on permissions. It’s a test quality/correctness issue, not a product behavior defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/FilterView.tsx:157 — The `key={key}` prop was dropped from GrafanaRuleListItem in a list that grows through load-more, which causes React key warnings and index-based reconciliation (per-row drawer/modal/clone state can attach to the wrong rule).

public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:83 — Ruler and prom abilities are OR-combined, so any disagreement fails open. If the prom payload lacks `provenance` (or the ruler path is loading or denies a rule as immutable), the prom path grants Pause/Delete/Duplicate/Export on rules the ruler path marks as provisioned or unsupported.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce OR-combined permission gating in `AlertRuleMenu` (e.g., `canPause = (rulerSupported&&rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported&&grafanaAllowed)`), which can “fail open” if the two ability sources disagree or one path is temporarily `NotSupported` (e.g., due to loading in the ruler-based hook) while the other returns allowed. However, the finding’s concrete scenario about missing `provenance` in the Prom payload can’t be verified from the diff: the PR adds `provenance?: string` to `GrafanaPromRuleDTO` and uses it in `isProvisionedPromRule`, but the diff doesn’t show the API response shape to confirm it can be absent in practice. So the concern is real and diff-grounded (the OR policy), but the claimed exploit/bug condition is not directly provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:324 — The prom path uses isAlertingRule for ModifyExport/Pause/Restore, whereas the ruler path used grafana.rule (which includes recording rules), so Grafana recording rules lose Export in the new list view.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (new prom-based abilities path), `ModifyExport`, `Pause`, and `Restore` are gated by `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` (so recording rules => `false`). Previously, the ruler-based path in `useAllRulerRuleAbilities` used `isGrafanaManagedAlertRule = rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)` for `ModifyExport`/`Pause`/`Restore`, which would be `true` for Grafana recording rules as well. Since list view now relies on the prom-based abilities hooks (e.g., `AlertRuleMenu` uses `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`), Grafana recording rules will no longer show Export (and related actions) in that context, i.e., a behavior regression introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:69 — Default mocks force useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities to [false,false], so the Grafana tests never exercise the ruler path and the cloud tests hide the skipToken Duplicate leak; the RBAC tests can pass while the real behavior is wrong.

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, `beforeEach` sets neutral defaults for both plural hooks (`useRulerRuleAbilities`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`) to return `[false,false]` for every requested action. In the Grafana RBAC tests, the setup then mainly overrides `useAlertRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (or the singular prom hook), but does not override `useRulerRuleAbilities`, even though `AlertRuleMenu` now ORs ruler-abilities and prom-abilities (`canX = (rulerSupported&&rulerAllowed) || (grafanaSupported&&grafanaAllowed)`). As a result, these tests don’t exercise the ruler-ability path at all, so regressions in the ruler side of `AlertRuleMenu` for Grafana rules could slip through. The part of the finding about a “skipToken Duplicate leak” or “real behavior is wrong” is not directly verifiable from this diff, but the reduced/imbalanced coverage due to the default mocks is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx:40 — The rule view href no longer includes `returnTo` (the old GrafanaRuleListItem used createReturnTo), so navigating back from a rule's page loses the list filter/scroll context.

In the deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`, `GrafanaRuleListItem` built `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })`, while the new `public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx` hardcodes `href: createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` (line ~40) with no `returnTo`. adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 — In the list view only promRule is passed (rule is undefined), so the silence drawer gate `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is always false: "Silence notifications" is now enabled by the prom ability but clicking it does nothing

adjudication.rationale: In the new list view path, Grafana rules are rendered via `GrafanaRuleListItem`, which calls `actions: <RuleActionsButtons promRule={rule} ... />` and does not pass the `rule` (RulerRuleDTO) prop (diff: `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`). At the same time, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` was updated to enable permissions via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(...)` when only `promRule` is present, meaning UI actions can become enabled even without a Ruler rule. However, the diff does not show any corresponding update to non-edit actions (like Silence) inside `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx` to use `promRule` for rule-type gating/behavior; only the Edit ability and identifier construction were adapted. (rule)` and thus becomes a no-op when `rule` is undefined, while the menu item is enabled by the new Prom-based ability logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:123 — Pause (line 123) and Delete (line 165) menu items still require `rulerRule`, which the list view no longer provides, so the new prom-based canPause/canDelete are never used and both actions disappear from the list view menu

public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:245 — useAllAlertRuleAbilities` (CombinedRule path) now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, where `isFederated` is hard-coded to false, so federated Mimir rule groups that used to be immutable via `isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)` now report Update/Delete as supported

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:325 — Pause, Restore, DeletePermanently and ModifyExport (line 324) in the prom path check `isAlertingRule`, while the ruler path used `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule` (which includes recording rules), so Grafana recording rules lose Pause and Export in the list view

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:287 — useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities copies almost all of useAllRulerRuleAbilities (immutability, MaybeSupported, abilities map), and the copies have already drifted: Pause/Restore/Export/DeletePermanently use isAlertingRule here but grafana.rule (which includes recording rules) in the ruler version.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:243 — The deprecated useAllAlertRuleAbilities now delegates to a path with a hardcoded `isFederated = false` plus commented-out code and a TODO, which silently drops the isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check that CombinedRule callers used to get.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:56 — Two parallel ability hooks with duplicate action lists, then ten destructures and five copies of the `(a && b) \|\| (c && d)` OR logic; this belongs in a single helper or one hook that picks the ruler or prom source.

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the diff introduces two parallel ability queries with the same action list: useRulerRuleAbilities(rulerRule, groupIdentifier, [Pause, Delete, Duplicate, Silence, ModifyExport]) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, [same actions]). adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:380 — The custom exported `skipToken` Symbol shares its name with RTK Query's skipToken, and it is only used by the prom hooks while the sibling ruler hooks accept `undefined`, so the API is inconsistent and confusing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces `export const skipToken = Symbol('ability-skip-token')` in `useAbilities.ts` and uses it in the new Grafana Prom rule ability hooks: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(rule: GrafanaPromRuleDTO | SkipToken, ...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(rule: GrafanaPromRuleDTO | SkipToken, ...)`. In contrast, the ruler counterpart `useRulerRuleAbilities` was changed to accept `rule: RulerRuleDTO | undefined` (no skip token), creating an API mismatch between “ruler” and “prom” hooks. Also, naming the exported symbol `skipToken` can realistically be confusing in a codebase that already commonly uses RTK Query’s `skipToken` name (even if RTK’s is not shown in this diff), since consumers now import `skipToken` from `../../hooks/useAbilities` (e.g., `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`, `RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx). adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:58 — Inline action array literals are passed to hooks that memoize on `[abilities, actions]`, so a new array every render defeats the useMemo.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:53 — Every list row now runs both the ruler and prom ability hook stacks here and again in the nested AlertRuleMenu (lines 58 and 73), which comes to 4 full ability computations per row, each with its own useFolder/config-status/useIsRuleEditable subscriptions, and the ruler path is pure waste in the list view because rulerRule is always undefined.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:289 — useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities subscribes to useFolder for the same folderUid twice (via useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable and again via useCanSilenceInFolder/useFolderPermissions), and it runs useGrafanaRulesSilenceSupport even when skipToken is passed, so skipToken never actually skips any subscription.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:58 — Inline action-array literals passed to useRulerRuleAbilities and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities (line 73) get a new identity every render, which defeats the `useMemo([abilities, actions])` in those hooks and returns fresh arrays for every row on every render.

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the calls to useRulerRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...]) and useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(..., [AlertRuleAction.Pause, ...]) pass inline array literals. In useAbilities.ts, both plural hooks memoize with dependencies [abilities, actions]; because the array literal is a new reference each render, the useMemo will recompute and return a new Ability[] each time, defeating memoization and potentially causing unnecessary per-row work in rule lists. adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:309 — With skipToken/undefined rule (all datasource-managed rules), useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities reports Duplicate as supported and gated only on the Grafana AlertingRuleCreate permission, and AlertRuleMenu.tsx:91 ORs this into canDuplicate, so users without the external-ruler write permission (or rules with no ruler/federated groups) now get Duplicate offered

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the Grafana abilities hook is invoked even when the promRule is not a Grafana-managed prom rule: `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(promRule) ? promRule : skipToken, ...)`, and its results are OR’ed into `canDuplicate` (and other `can*`). In useAbilities.ts, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(skipToken, ...)` calls `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined)`, and that implementation sets `MaybeSupported = loading ? NotSupported : AlwaysSupported` and then `Duplicate` uses `toAbility(duplicateSupported, rulesPermissions.create)` without requiring a real rule/folder context. This makes it possible for `grafanaDuplicateSupported` to be treated as supported (and potentially allowed via Grafana create permission) even though the rule is not a Grafana prom rule, and then the OR in AlertRuleMenu can expose “Duplicate” when the ruler-based ability is false.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rule-viewer/AlertRuleMenu.tsx:84 — OR-combining ruler and prom abilities lets the weaker prom-based immutability check (promRule.provenance, a new DTO field with no backend change in this diff) override a ruler-based "provisioned" NotSupported, so provisioned rules can show Pause/Delete when both rule sources are passed (e.g. rule viewer)

adjudication.rationale: In AlertRuleMenu.tsx the PR changes permission gating to OR-combine abilities from `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)` (e.g. `canPause = (pauseSupported && pauseAllowed) || (grafanaPauseSupported && grafanaPauseAllowed)`). In `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, immutability/provisioning is determined via `isProvisionedPromRule(rule)` which depends on the new optional `GrafanaPromRuleDTOBase.provenance?: string` field. This diff adds that field but does not show any corresponding backend/population change, so `provenance` may be undefined for provisioned rules, causing prom-based abilities to treat them as mutable/supported. With the OR logic, those prom-based “allowed” results can override the ruler-based `NotSupported` for provisioned rules when both `rulerRule` and `promRule` are provided to the menu (as the component API allows), making provisioned rules incorrectly show actions like Pause/Delete.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:287 — New useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities/useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable/useGrafanaPromRuleAbilit(y|ies) have no unit tests for provisioned, plugin-provided, recording rules, missing folderUid, folder-loading, or no-permission cases.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `useAbilities.ts` (`useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`, `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable`, `skipToken`, `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility/Abilities`) including new branches for provisioned Prom rules (`isProvisionedPromRule`), plugin-provided rules, alerting-vs-recording behavior (`prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule`), and folder-based permission evaluation with early returns when `rule`/`folderUid`/`folder` are missing or loading. The updated tests (e.g., `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx` and `RulesTable.test.tsx`) exercise some permission outcomes via UI (including a no-edit-permission case), but the diff does not show targeted tests covering several newly introduced edge branches the finding lists (provisioned/plugin-provided/recording, missing `folderUid`, folder-loading). So the core concern—new nontrivial ability logic lacks broad test coverage—is diff-grounded, though the statement that there are no tests for no-permission cases is not fully accurate because at least one UI test covers lack of edit permission.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:207 — Test asserts exactly 4 menu items with full update/delete permissions granted, locking in the regression that Pause and Delete never render in the list view (AlertRuleMenu still gates them on rulerRule, which is now always undefined); ui.menuItems.delete is defined but never used.

AlertRuleMenu.tsx was explicitly changed to compute abilities from both `useRulerRuleAbilities(...)` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(...)` and then OR them (e.g., `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)`). So Pause/Delete are not exclusively gated on `rulerRule` anymore. While the test does assert `menuItems.length === 4` and `ui.menuItems.delete` is defined but unused, the diff alone does not verify that Delete/Pause “never render” or that the test is locking in such a regression; that’s speculative without seeing AlertRuleMenu’s item composition.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:194 — Test only checks the Silence menu item exists and never clicks it, so it misses that the silence drawer can't open in the list view (RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:104 requires a rulerRule).

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/hooks/useAbilities.ts:245 — useAllAlertRuleAbilities/useAllRulerRuleAbilities now hardcode isFederated=false (was isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)), so federated Mimir rules become editable/deletable, and no test covers this behavior change.

adjudication.rationale: In `useAbilities.ts`, `useAllRulerRuleAbilities()` now sets `isFederated = false` unconditionally (with a TODO) where previously the federated check existed (`isFederatedRuleGroup(...)` was imported before and is no longer used). Since `immutableRule` is computed as `isProvisioned || isFederated || isPluginProvided`, this change removes the federated-rule immutability guard and can make federated Mimir rules eligible for Update/Delete if `useIsRuleEditable()` returns editable/removable. adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:105 — Grafana-rule RBAC tests now mock useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities and leave useRulerRuleAbilities at the default [false,false], so they only check mock wiring, never cover the ruler path for Grafana rules, and never test the new OR logic (ruler denies but prom allows, or the reverse).

adjudication.rationale: In `RulesTable.test.tsx`, the `beforeEach` sets default neutral mocks where `useRulerRuleAbilities` returns `[false,false]` for every action. In the Grafana-rule RBAC tests, the overrides primarily mock `useAlertRuleAbility` and `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` (and sometimes `useGrafanaPromRuleAbility`), but do not override `useRulerRuleAbilities` for Grafana rules. Since `AlertRuleMenu` now computes `canX` via OR between ruler-abilities and prom-abilities (e.g., `canDelete = (deleteSupported && deleteAllowed) || (grafanaDeleteSupported && grafanaDeleteAllowed)` in `AlertRuleMenu.tsx`), these tests exercise only the prom side (with ruler side fixed false) and never validate the new OR behavior in mixed cases (ruler allows/prom denies or vice versa). adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/components/rules/RulesTable.test.tsx:85 — useGrafanaPromRuleAbility is mocked, but no component rendered by RulesTable uses it (RuleActionsButtons uses useAlertRuleAbility), so this mock is dead setup that makes the test look like it covers more than it does.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/components/RuleActionsButtons.V2.tsx:66 — The new promRule-only branches (getEditableIdentifier returning undefined leads to a null render, and getIsProvisioned from promRule.provenance used for duplicate) have no tests.

This is a specific, diff-grounded test gap rather than a demonstrated runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/FilterView.tsx:157 — FilterView now renders GrafanaRuleListItem directly without ruler data and without the previous key prop, and no test covers the Grafana branch of the filter view.

The claim about lacking test coverage for this specific Grafana FilterView branch is not directly verifiable from the diff alone (no FilterView tests are shown/modified), but the missing `key` is a concrete, diff-grounded review issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx:79 — The href assertion uses stringContaining, so it can't catch that GrafanaRuleListItem dropped the returnTo query param from the rule view link.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `GrafanaRuleListItem`’s link changed from `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` (deleted `GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx`) to `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`)` (new `GrafanaRuleListItem.tsx`), i.e., the `returnTo` query param is no longer added. In `GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx`, the href check uses `toHaveAttribute('href', expect.stringContaining(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`))`, which would still pass even if the query string was dropped. That’s a concrete test-gap tied to this change (it won’t detect this regression/behavior change), but the diff alone doesn’t prove the missing `returnTo` is definitively a functional bug in all contexts.
